subject: RE: OptiRetail - streaming parse failures impacting throughput and latency
messages:
From: ops+alerts@optiretail.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [ALERT] 20% error spike + 3x latency on Inference stream

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing a spike in errors and a large latency increase on the streaming endpoint this morning around 08:50 PST. Error rate climbed to ~18% and median token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~360ms. Throughput for our burst traffic dropped ~40%. Attached is a short pcap and an example error trace.

We rolled back to the previous minor version and saw the error rate drop back down, but we'd like an RCA and a long-term fix — this is on our path to production for a large holiday push. Alice Jones (VP Eng) is cc'd.

- OptiRetail Ops

Attachments: sample-request.pcap (pcap), error_trace.json (text)

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [ALERT] 20% error spike + 3x latency on Inference stream

I've reproduced locally with OptiRetail's sample pcap. Symptoms: intermittent parser failures when chunked/partial header frames arrive split across network packets; the client SDK's streaming parser emits a premature EOF and retries, which causes request duplication and backpressure on the runtime leading to higher tail latency. The rollback they mentioned removed a recent change in the SDK that relaxed header validation.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Ask OptiRetail to pin to the previous SDK minor release (quick, but not ideal).
- Turn on server-side de-duplication/time-window dedupe for streaming connectors (requires a canary; low-code but may add overhead).
- Patch SDK parser to buffer partial header fragments for up to 50ms before treating them as terminal — we can hotfix and publish a patch within 24-48h.

I'll start a JIRA and run the parser instrumented across our canary fleet. Need decision on which path to recommend to the customer.

Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Thanks Marcus — solid repro. Short-term we should:
- Tell OptiRetail to pin to SDK v1.14.2 (their rollback) and disable the relaxed header validation flag; include a doc snippet and quick command.
- I'll draft an exec note for Alice outlining impact, mitigation, and ETA for fix.

For the hotfix: prioritize a parser patch that buffers partial headers by default and include a toggle for strict validation. Rishi, can you scope the canary for server dedupe? We'd like a fallback if clients can't upgrade immediately.

I want the hotfix target in 36 hours and a canary rollout within 8 hours after that. Jordan, please let the customer know we have a clear remediation plan and a patch timeline.

- Stephanie

Subject: RE: [ALERT] 20% error spike + 3x latency on Inference stream

Hi Alice / OptiRetail team — thanks for the quick flag. We're on this as P0. TL;DR: we've identified the likely root cause as a client SDK change that relaxed header validation and can cause the streaming parser to emit premature EOFs when header frames arrive split across packets. That in turn causes retries and backend backpressure which explains the increased error rate and latency.

Immediate actions:
- Please pin to SDK v1.14.2 (the version you've already rolled back to). We recommend not upgrading to the v1.15.x line until we ship a parser patch.
- Our engineering team will ship a parser hotfix within ~36 hours. We'll provide a canary rollout plan and a server-side dedupe fallback within 8 hours of the patch if needed.

We're treating this as high priority and will share a brief executive note within the hour. I've cc'd our Reliability and Runtime leads.

Jordan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Attachments: canary-rollout-plan.pdf (pdf)

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
To: alice.jones@optiretail.com, ops+alerts@optiretail.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: OptiRetail incident update + exec note

Alice / OptiRetail leadership,

Quick incident update and executive summary:

What happened
- A recent client SDK change relaxed streaming header validation. Under certain network conditions where header frames are fragmented across TCP packets the SDK's streaming parser could treat an incomplete header as a terminal condition and trigger a retry. The retries produced duplicate streams and increased load on our inference runtime, causing higher error rates and elevated tail latency for OptiRetail's bursts.

Impact
- Peak error rate ~18% (reproduced from logs and customer pcap)
- Median token latency increase from ~120ms to ~360ms during the incident window
- Throughput observed to drop ~35-45% for bursty traffic patterns

Remediation delivered
- Customer rollback to SDK v1.14.2 stabilized immediately (short-term).
- We shipped SDK patch v1.15.1 at 08:35 PST today which: buffers partial header fragments for up to 60ms, adds robust header reassembly, and re-enables strict-by-default validation with a toggle.
- We performed a controlled canary across 10% of streaming connectors and verified error rate and latency returned to baseline for the canary cohort.
- Server-side dedupe option (JIRA-INF-3421) is available as a short-term mitigation if a customer cannot upgrade immediately.

Next steps
- We recommend OptiRetail schedule SDK upgrade to v1.15.1 in a staged rollout; we've provided a migration guide and a roll-forward playbook.
- Follow-up post-mortem will include timeline, root cause analysis, and additional telemetry to detect early signs of partial-header fragmentation.

If you'd like a call to walk through the plan and the canary results, we can make time tomorrow. Jordan will coordinate scheduling and procurement next steps if you need a short-term support arrangement.

Sincerely,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (docx)
